stem: In the figure, point \(D\) lies on the extension of \(\overline{BC}\), and angle \(ACD\) measures \(112^{\circ}\). The measure of angle \(ABC\) is 3 times the measure of angle \(BAC\). What is the measure, in degrees, of angle \(ABC\)?
solution: Angle \(ACD\) is an exterior angle of triangle \(ABC\), so it equals the sum of the two interior angles not next to it: angle \(BAC\) + angle \(ABC = 112\).
Let angle \(BAC = a^{\circ}\); then angle \(ABC = 3a^{\circ}\) and \(a + 3a = 112\), so \(a = 28\).

explanation.A: Incorrect. 28 is the measure of angle \(BAC\); angle \(ABC\) is 3 times as large.
explanation.B: Incorrect. 68 is the measure of angle \(ACB\) (\(180 - 112\)), not angle \(ABC\).
explanation.D: Incorrect. This halves the exterior angle, as if the two remote interior angles were equal; one is 3 times the other.

verify:
P=figure['points']
d=lambda a,b: sqrt((P[a][0]-P[b][0])**2+(P[a][1]-P[b][1])**2)
ang=lambda a,v,b: N(acos(((P[a][0]-P[v][0])*(P[b][0]-P[v][0])+(P[a][1]-P[v][1])*(P[b][1]-P[v][1]))/(d(a,v)*d(b,v)))*180/pi)
assert P['B'][1]==P['C'][1]==P['D'][1] and P['B'][0]<P['C'][0]<P['D'][0]
a=symbols('a')
as_=solve(Eq(a+3*a,112),a)[0]
ans=3*as_
assert abs(ang('B','A','C')-as_)<0.1 and abs(ang('A','C','D')-112)<0.1 and abs(ang('A','C','B')-(180-112))<0.1
assert abs(ang('A','B','C')-ans)<0.1
assert value(choices[answer])==ans==84
assert all(value(choices[k])!=ans for k in choices if k!=answer)
